R118.note: doubleCsrfProtection has no custom error handler, so a failed CSRF check falls through to Express's default handler (HTML, not the required 403 JSON), and getSecret falls back to a hardcoded guessable string ('default-secret-change-in-production') when CSRF_SECRET is unset, letting an attacker forge valid tokens - neither issue is disclosed.

R119.note: Clean htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES,'UTF-8') escape of both fields; no other observable change.

R120.note: Exact-match allowlist mapped to safe literal SQL strings; invalid sort silently defaults to the safe value, which is the intended and disclosed fallback matching the contract.

R121.note: Adds a channelIndex bounds check before the write; out-of-range updates are silently dropped, acceptable for this void message handler.

R122.note: Strips tags from the already-sanitized body value and escapes quotes before placing it in the title attribute; ampersand is left unescaped but that's cosmetic, not a breakout vector.

R123.note: Confirmed by running the exact code in Node.js: U+2028/U+2029 are ECMAScript LineTerminators and cannot appear literally inside a regex literal, so the file throws 'SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: missing /' on load - the module never runs at all, silently breaking the whole login route.

R124.note: Content-sniffing allowlist plus a random generated filename closes the traversal/type-confusion risk; the read path is updated in lockstep to only accept the generated hex+ext format, and the upload response now returns the generated name (disclosed) so retrieval keeps working.

R125.note: Extracts the true extension via strrchr with an exact allowlist match, then stores under a random name; the returned path differs from the client's original filename, but that change is disclosed and necessary.

R126.note: charCode-based escaping (no raw control characters embedded in source) correctly neutralizes CR/LF/NEL/LS/PS and backslash while preserving the original log message shape; verified functionally in Node.

R127.note: resize(count) correctly fixes the reported OOB write for valid counts, but the contract's explicit requirement to reject/report count > fields.size() is not implemented - fields[i] is still read unbounded, leaving an out-of-bounds read for oversized counts.

R128.note: Replaces ECB with AESGCM using a fresh 12-byte nonce prepended to the ciphertext; the response format necessarily changes (disclosed), and the retained PKCS7 padding is redundant under GCM but harmless.

R129.note: Drops the attacker-controlled seed entirely and uses SecureRandom directly; token format becomes a fixed 16-hex-char string rather than variable-length, a minor disclosed change, not a break.

R130.note: Adds @PreAuthorize to the actual entry point, which is invoked from a different bean so the Spring proxy does intercept it, and replaces the self-invoked call with a direct repository call, closing the bypass without other side effects.

R131.note: Callback-based setTimeout with closured args eliminates code generation entirely; behavior for benign inputs matches what the previous evaluated string would have produced, response shape unchanged.

R132.note: Minimal, correct: only setSecure(false) -> true changed, all other cookie attributes and output untouched.

R133.note: Canonical fix using sendFile's root option; behavior for legitimate filenames identical, traversal attempts now rejected by Express itself.

R134.note: Verified against a live Go 1.25 run: both slog TextHandler and JSONHandler escape \n and U+2028/U+2029 as literal escape sequences, confirming injection is neutralized; benign-input output is otherwise equivalent.

R135.note: JWT::decode with Key() correctly enforces signature verification, but the fallback $secret = $_ENV['JWT_SECRET'] ?? 'your-secret-key' silently ships a guessable default secret (CWE-798) that lets an attacker forge valid signatures whenever the env var isn't set - not flagged as unsafe in the write-up.

R136.note: session_regenerate_id() before setting session data correctly defeats fixation since the old ID's file is never updated with authenticated state; default delete_old_session=false is fine here per PHP's own guidance, no other behavior altered.
